scope: Core Deferred/lifetime test sufficiency only; read-only review before implementation

findings.title: Observer registration never races settlement, leaving the cleanup lease subscription race untested
findings.evidence: concurrentResolveRejectAndLateSubscriptionSettleOnce registers its initial onSettled/onRejected callbacks before submitting settlement tasks; the late onSettled callback is registered only after all resolve/reject futures have joined. The join-other-subscriber test registers only after settlement notification has begun. A check-then-register implementation can lose an observer between reading pending state and insertion yet pass these tests. Core request ownership relies on settlement notification to release pending work, so this is a meaningful leak path rather than an extra feature.
findings.requestedChange: Add bounded barrier-started concurrent registrations of onSettled and onRejected against resolve/reject, retaining per-listener counters and the actual winning outcome/error identity. After joining every future, assert every settlement observer ran exactly once; rejection observers ran exactly once iff reject won, and never for resolve. Include repeated settlement and late registrations to verify no loss or duplication. Keep callbacks observable outside fail-soft observer assertions (capture callback failures for final assertion). A core test settling returned Deferred on another thread during callback return is a useful integration counterpart, but is not required to close this finding if the public primitive race is directly covered.

positiveAssessment: Preserved RED log shows all32 tests executed and failed: absent Deferred/AsyncRouteHandler APIs and actual existing cleanup/lifecycle/StackOverflow defects, without skipped tests or fabricated success.
Explicit ownership tests require response finish to retain pending Deferred resources, multiple results to retain independent leases, and resolution alone to avoid implicit next/end.
Active and queued callbacks retain upload ownership, abort cancels pending leases, repeated/late actions cannot double-clean, and normal completion is distinguished from detected abort.

Tests cover failure identity/error cursor, fail-soft observers, late callbacks, mounted request identity, JSON/stream/SSE completion, service shutdown, grace/deadline and restored lifecycle request context.
Concurrent completion/abort, cross-thread next joins and deep synchronous chain provide meaningful bounded execution checks.
